# Wave 1, Task 1: Initial CR, Repair, Rerouted SR/CR, and Fold

Checkout: `/workspace/project` (the branch checkout). `REPORT_DIR=/tmp/reports`.

Transcript observation: `wave 1 base 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`

## 1. Initial CR (wave-level, over the integrated diff)

Stage every deliverable, then record the review tree. Run the full `fix-delta-tree-shell` block with `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'`.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell block, FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_CR1>
```

Print `wave 1 review cr1 tree <T_CR1>`. Use the printed SHA, not this placeholder. Stop on a nonzero exit.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"]" }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```

Observed result: `wave 1 task 1 verdict FIX_FIRST report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md`. This is CR review 1, so there is no trajectory yet.

- `behaviourChange: true` triggers the behaviour-change reroute: SR first, then CR.
- `touchedTasks: [1]` means the repair belongs to task 1.
- Next action: fix 1.

## 2. Repair (one in-place implementer, never a nested worktree)

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md - read it yourself before repairing." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }] })
```

- The payload has no `worktree: true` and no commit or staging instruction.
- Observed: `wave 1 task 1 status DONE report /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md patch n/a (in-place)`.
- The worker committed at `2222…`, so HEAD moved. This does not matter, because the Fix delta compares tree objects, not a SHA range or the working tree.

Rerun the scoped gate (observed: pass):

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) >"/tmp/reports/gate-0.log" 2>&1
```

## 3. Rerouted SR (first in the reroute; its ordinal continues the SR count)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell block, FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_SR2>
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_SR2>   # emptiness check only
```

Print `wave 1 review sr2 tree <T_SR2>`.

The repair-only delta is `<T_CR1>` → `<T_SR2>`. It covers `src/parse.mjs` and `tests/error.test.mjs`. It excludes the original wave content, even though the worker's commit moved HEAD.

Shape of this SR dispatch:
- It is review 2 of the task's SR loop, because the initial SR was review 1.
- It runs against the integrated checkout, not a snapshot.
- It carries no test commands.
- It has no `## Previous review report` marker, so the reviewer emits no `TRAJECTORY:` line.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "spec-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md. Review the integrated checkout against the anchored task and spec; never run tests.\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_SR2>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_SR2> yourself." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["NEEDS_REWORK", "OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES"] } }] })
```

Observed: `wave 1 task 1 verdict COMPLIANT report /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md`.

## 4. CR re-review (only after the SR is COMPLIANT)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell block, FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_CR2>
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_CR2>
```

Print `wave 1 review cr2 tree <T_CR2>`. The CR delta is keyed by wave, from the prior CR's tree `<T_CR1>` to `<T_CR2>`.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"]\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md - read it yourself.\n<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md>\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_CR2>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_CR2> yourself." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```

- `BASE_SHA` stays `1111…` and `HEAD_SHA` stays `WORKTREE`. The whole-diff source therefore still includes the worker's committed repair.
- Observed: `wave 1 task 1 verdict SHIP report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md`. This is a clean review, so the loop ends. A clean report has no trajectory to consume.

## 5. Fold and commit, only after SR COMPLIANT and CR SHIP

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 \
  && git -C /workspace/project add -A \
  && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: <task title from manifest heading>"
```

`reset --soft` folds the worker's commit `2222…` together with all staged deliverables into one wave commit:
- `src/parse.mjs`
- `tests/parse.test.mjs`
- `tests/error.test.mjs`

If the commit is empty, stop instead of completing the task.

After the commit, run `plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 0, status: "complete" })`. Then execute any explicit manifest `orchestrator` instruction once; the scenario names none. The tree is now clean for the next wave.

## Empty repair delta

An empty `diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_SR2>` means the repair changed no tracked file. This includes ignored-only edits, and it holds even though the worker made a commit, because a commit without content change produces the same tree.

In that case:
1. Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
2. Count it as a failed attempt under "When a Subagent Fails".
3. Re-dispatch the in-place implementer with `/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md` and the note "your fix changed no tracked file".
4. If the second attempt is also empty or fails, stop with a stop note. Task 1 stays `in_progress`.

Below is the prescribed sequence, not a claim of execution. Schema identifiers refer to the exact schemas supplied in the dispatch contract. `$T0`, `$T1`, and `$T2` denote actual tree IDs printed by the captures—not invented IDs.

### 1. Stage and capture the initial CR tree

Keep the wave base fixed even if a worker later commits:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD
printf 'wave 1 base 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111\n'
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Run this **entire capture block** before the initial CR, saving its printed SHA as `T0` in orchestration state:

```bash
FD_ROOT=/workspace/project
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Record:

```text
wave 1 review 1 tree /workspace/project
```

```js
    }],

  }]

```

Consume the supplied JSON:

```text
wave 1 task 1 verdict FIX_FIRST report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md
```

`behaviourChange: true` requires SR before CR after repair; `touchedTasks: [1]` identifies the SR owner.

### 2. One in-place repair

```js
subagent({
  async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",

/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md
Read and address the findings yourself. Report test-contract evidence and an explicit implementer status.`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] }
  }]
})
```

No nested worktree, patch integration, or commit instruction. The supplied worker outcome is:

```text
wave 1 task 1 status DONE report /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md
```

Its reported commit is `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`; that does **not** replace the wave base.

Rerun the consuming scoped gate:

```bash
(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) >/tmp/reports/gate-1-repair.log 2>&1
```

After the supplied passing result:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Run the entire capture block again; retain its SHA as `T1`. Check:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat "$T0" "$T1"
```

### 3. Behavior-change SR, then CR

```text
wave 1 review 2 tree /workspace/project
```

Dispatch SR as a **first review of this repair**, without a previous-review marker or test commands:

```js
subagent({
  async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "spec-reviewer",
      output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md
anchor: "### Task 1:"
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md
Spec anchors: lines 8-10
Implementer report: /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md
Read anchored requirements and Rules yourself. Review the repair in this integrated checkout; never execute tests.
## Fix delta
tree-before: <actual T0>
tree-after: <actual T1>
Run git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <actual T0> <actual T1> to read the repair-only delta.`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["NEEDS_REWORK", "OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES"] }
  }]
})
```

At the supplied boundary:

```text
wave 1 task 1 verdict COMPLIANT report /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md
```

Stage and run the entire capture block again, recording `T2`:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

```text
wave 1 review 3 tree /workspace/project
```

Dispatch CR using the initial CR carrier shape, output `/tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md`, unchanged base, `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`, anchors, spec, and scoped command array. Add:

```text
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md
Read the prior report yourself.
## Fix delta
tree-before: <actual T0>
tree-after: <actual T2>
Run git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <actual T0> <actual T2>.
If issues remain, emit the prescribed TRAJECTORY line and structured trajectory:
STAGNANT for materially unchanged prior Critical/Moderate findings;
otherwise DIVERGING for nondecreasing counts or new Critical/Moderate findings;
otherwise CONVERGING with counts and maximum severity.
```

Consume verdict, required `behaviourChange`, and any applicable trajectory from JSON. Supplied outcome:

```text
wave 1 task 1 verdict SHIP report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md
```

### 4. Only now fold and complete

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "fix: validate numeric input"
```

After successful, nonempty commit:

```js
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 1, status: "complete" })
```

An empty `T0..T1` repair delta means no tracked repair: dispatch no re-review, count a failed attempt, and redispatch with the prior report and “your fix changed no tracked file,” subject to the two-attempt limit. Stop here.

# Wave 1, singleton code wave: CR, repair, SR, CR, fold

**Fixed values**
- Checkout: `/workspace/project` (branch checkout, already integrated)
- `REPORT_DIR=/tmp/reports`
- planPath `/workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md`, anchor `### Task 1:`
- Spec `/workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md`

Transcript line already printed: `wave 1 base 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.

## 1. Initial CR (CR review 1)

Stage everything, then capture the review tree:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Run the `fix-delta-tree-shell` block with `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'`. Record its printed SHA as `T_CR1`, keyed to wave 1. Print `wave 1 review cr1 tree <T_CR1>`.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"]" }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```

**Observed result:** `wave 1 task 1 verdict FIX_FIRST report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md patch none`
- `behaviourChange: true`, so the reroute is SR first, then CR.
- `touchedTasks: [1]`.
- This is review 1, so there is no trajectory. Next step is fix 1.

## 2. Repair (fix 1, in place)

The worker runs in the branch checkout. It gets no `worktree`, no nested wave, and no commit or staging instruction.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md - read it yourself before repairing." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }] })
```

**Observed result:** `wave 1 task 1 status DONE report /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md patch none`
- The worker committed `2222…`, so HEAD moved.
- `WAVE_BASE_SHA` stays `1111…`.
- The fix delta is computed from tree objects, so the worker's commit does not affect it.

Rerun the scoped gate. Per the observation, it passes:

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) >"/tmp/reports/gate-0.log" 2>&1
```

## 3. SR first (behaviour-change reroute: SR review 2)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Rerun the `fix-delta-tree-shell` block with `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'` and record the result as `T_SR2`, keyed to task 1. Print `wave 1 review sr2 tree <T_SR2>`.

Check for an empty delta:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_SR2>
```

The SR payload follows these rules:
- No `## Previous review report` marker, because this is a first-review shape with no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- Its ordinal continues the task's SR count, so this is SR review 2.
- It carries no commands.
- `cwd` is the integrated checkout, not a snapshot.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "spec-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md. Repair report: /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md. Review the integrated checkout; never run tests.\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_SR2>\nRun: git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_SR2>" }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["NEEDS_REWORK", "OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES"] } }] })
```

**Observed result:** `wave 1 task 1 verdict COMPLIANT report /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md patch none`

## 4. CR re-review (CR review 2)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Rerun the `fix-delta-tree-shell` block and record `T_CR2`, keyed to wave 1. Print `wave 1 review cr2 tree <T_CR2>`. Then check:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_CR2>
```

The re-review keeps `BASE_SHA` at `1111…` and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` even though HEAD is now `2222…`. Because the reviewer reads the checkout against Base, the delta includes the committed repair plus anything staged.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md - read it yourself.\n<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md>\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_CR2>\nRun: git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_CR2>" }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```

**Observed result:** `wave 1 task 1 verdict SHIP report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md patch none`
- A clean review omits the `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- The loop ends.

## 5. Fold and complete (only after COMPLIANT and SHIP)

Fold the base, the worker's commit `2222…` and the staged state into one wave commit:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 && \
git -C /workspace/project add -A && \
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: <title>"
```

Then:
1. If the commit would be empty, stop instead.
2. Call `plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <task 1 index>, status: "complete" })`.
3. Run any explicit manifest `orchestrator` instruction once.
4. Record the next wave's base with `git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD`.

`tests/error.test.mjs` is a new file, but it does not enter `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS`. That list stays the manifest union.

## What an empty repair delta would mean

An empty delta means `diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_SR2>` (or `<T_CR2>`) shows nothing. This includes a repair that touched only ignored files. It means the fix changed no tracked file, regardless of any worker commit or message.

When that happens:
- Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
- Count it as a failed attempt under "When a Subagent Fails".
- Resend the repair with `/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md` and the note "your fix changed no tracked file".
- After the second failed attempt, stop with a stop note.
- Task 1 stays `in_progress`, and nothing is committed.

Otherwise the gauntlet-style transcript lines (wave base, status/verdict/report/patch, tree observations) are an improvement and deliver the Change cleanly.
